subject: Error in gpa for specimens after unbending...

messages.author: 6fd1fccedadfe847
messages.subject: Error in gpa for specimens after unbending...
parts:
Hi everyone,
I used the unbending tool in tpsUtil (both quadratic and cubic), but gpa in geomorph wouldn't work. It gives an error: "Coordinates must be a 3D array". When I checked the data I found out that many negative values in the tps file were translated to NA (for both quadratic and cubic).
Does anyone have an idea how to overcome this (should I just add the most negative value to all values - making the most negative equal zero)?
Thanks in advance,
Avi

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in gpa for specimens after unbending...
parts:
Avi, 

When you use tools outside of geomorph and bring data into geomorph, you have to ensure that they are formatted properly. The error message is because it appears you are trying to use data not arranged in an array. 

This does not appear to be a missing data error. That might also be an issue but check the data class you are using first. 

Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in gpa for specimens after unbending...
parts:
Hi Mike,
In parallel to trying to do gpa to the unbent quadratic and cubic, I was successful in doing gpa to the tps file before unbending. All of those 3 arrays (I verified the class) were loaded to R using readland.tps and that step went well for all three, resulting num[1:72,1:2,1:273] for all three. The only difference that I can see are the NA instead of numeric values almost in all specimens - only in the unbent arrays. Is it possible that the gpa function interpret many NA values as a missing dimension? If not, what else can it be?
Avi

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error in gpa for specimens after unbending...
parts:
Hi all,
Not asking any question this time, but only updating on a solution I found.
Although readland.tps can't deal with negative values, converting the tps to csv using tpsUtil helps here. Now you can do one of two: 1. add the minimum value to all coordinates and then use 'arrayspecs', 2. skip the adding minimum value to all coordinates and just use 'arrayspecs'. In both ways the 'gpagen' gives the exact same results.
Avi
